items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Sidney asked if I'd go in with him with a quartet, the wonderful Kenny Kersey on piano and Vic Dickenson on trombone, and myself.

ctx.x: Hey George, that was quite some saga. That Ben Gassy saga from the Washington era, you being a horseman and all -- sorry about that horse and you!

On 52nd Street, I worked the other side of the coin, as they say. I went into the so-called Dixieland oriented club of Jimmy Ryan's across the street from the Three Deuces. I hadn't known Sidney previously, I believe Jimmy Ryan himself asked me or recommended me to Sidney, and Sidney asked if I'd go in with him with a quartet, the wonderful Kenny Kersey on piano and Vic Dickenson on trombone, and myself.
I consider myself lucky to have the ability to go from a Webster oriented group to work with and please a traditional New Orleans legend.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: the band personnel started out, Buck Clayton on trumpet, Bennie Morton on trombone, Eddie Barefield, and Ken Kersey.

ctx.x: a Dixieland band. I don't think anybodie that hears this or any musician was aware of what was happening then. And if they hear this interview, they will certainly get a laugh out of it.

Anyway, Ben borrowed some Dixieland arrangements from somebody, and we went in and we went to rehearsal, which was up in Eddie Barefield's studio on 48th Street -- and the band personnel started out, Buck Clayton on trumpet, Bennie Morton on trombone, Eddie Barefield, and Ken Kersey. However, I have to say first, as we went to the rehearsal, he hadn't hired Kenny yet and we rehearsed first, without Kenny, and somebody suggested that Monk --Thelonius Monk -- was at Linton's and he was out for awhile and he could…

Excuse me for interrupting again, Cliff. But I think for the record we might as well let them know that the studio you were rehearsing in was Eddie Barefield who was a saxophone player. And the piano player - and Ken Kersey was a pianist so they would know who Ken Kersey was -- he was a pianist, the late Ken Kersey, and of course, everybody knows he played piano. Please carry on.
